title: Azure Logic Apps: Built-in vs Managed Azure Blob Storage Connector.
summary: Azure Logic Apps offer two versions of the Azure Blob Storage Connector: built-in connectors that run natively in the Logic Apps runtime, and managed connectors deployed in Azure. The built-in version processes all existing blobs on first execution then new/updated files, while the managed version ignores existing files and only works in root folders, affecting workflow behavior and security when virtual networks are involved.
key_points: Built-in connectors execute directly within Azure Logic Apps runtime while managed connectors are hosted in Azure and run on shared clusters
Azure Blob Storage built-in connector processes existing blobs first, then subsequent new/modified files; managed connector ignores existing files and subfolders
When using virtual networks, managed connectors execute outside the VNet on shared clusters while built-in connectors run within the same VNet as the Logic App
Selecting the wrong connector type can cause unexpected problems when moving workflows between Consumption and Standard Logic App plans
